en.headline: ERB to launch AI courses for working people from November
en.dek: Financial Secretary Paul Chan said the Employees Retraining Board will partner with major technology firms to offer specialised artificial-intelligence training as part of a HK$50 million two-year programme aiming to reach 50,000 people.
body: Financial Secretary Paul Chan wrote in his weekly blog on Sunday that the Employees Retraining Board will collaborate with large technology companies to roll out professional AI courses for working adults starting in November.

The initiative forms part of the “AI for All” training programme funded with HK$50 million in the Budget, which targets more than 200 activities over two years and is expected to benefit about 50,000 participants. Cyberport, Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation and the Hong Kong Productivity Council are also involved in delivering modules for students, the public and professionals.

Chan noted that rapid advances in artificial intelligence continue to reshape the job market and stressed the need for young people to acquire relevant skills early. He cited a survey indicating that nearly 70 per cent of Hong Kong respondents already use AI tools proficiently, while about 20 per cent are “super users” who automate daily tasks with AI agents.

zh.headline: 陳茂波：僱員再培訓局11月起為在職人士推出AI課程
zh.dek: 財政司司長在網誌表示，再培訓局將與大型科企合作推出專業人工智能課程，屬五千萬元「全民AI培訓」計劃一部分，兩年目標惠及約五萬人次。
body: 財政司司長陳茂波周日在網誌表示，僱員再培訓局將與大型科技企業合作，由11月起為全港在職人士推出專業人工智能課程。
有關安排屬今年初《財政預算案》撥款5,000萬元的「全民AI培訓」計劃一部分。計劃目標在今明兩年舉辦超過200項活動，預計惠及約5萬人次。數碼港、香港科技園公司及香港生產力促進局亦會參與，為學生、市民及在職人士提供不同培訓模組。
陳茂波指出，人工智能技術發展迅速，將持續為就業市場帶來挑戰，必須加快準備，讓年輕人及早掌握新技能。他引述調查指，本港近七成受訪市民已能熟練使用AI工具，約兩成屬「超級用戶」，懂得利用AI智能體自動化處理日常任務。
